project.title: EHR Adoption and Medicaid Incentive Program Evaluation
project.research_question: Did earlier state Medicaid EHR incentive program launches lead to greater EHR adoption?

dataset.source: ONC Health IT Adoption and Use dataset
dataset.outcome: Proportion of hospitals with basic EHR adoption

policy.name: Medicaid EHR Incentive Program
policy.source: CMS State EHR Incentive Program Web Resources Guide, January 2017
policy.treatment_definition: State Medicaid program registration launch year

did_analysis.interpretation: The early-launch cohort had approximately 0.22 percentage points less adoption growth than the later-launch cohort. The difference was not statistically significant.

psm_analysis.method: Logistic regression propensity scores and one-to-one matching
psm_analysis.interpretation: Matched early-launch states had 6.29 percentage points less adoption growth than matched later-launch states during 2010–2011. The confidence interval includes zero.

limitations: Observational analysis does not establish causality.
Parallel trends cannot be proven from observed pre-treatment data.
Only seven matched state pairs were available.
Propensity score matching used only historical EHR adoption variables.
National HITECH policies affected states in both groups.
Annual EHR adoption data may not align with exact program launch months.
Matched and unmatched DID estimates target different state populations.
The confidence intervals do not rule out meaningful positive or negative effects.
